candidates.title: reviewerBackends re-walks the same chain-skip loop ReviewBudgetTimeout already owns
candidates.detail: internal/config/config.go:113-126 (Backends.ReviewBudgetTimeout) already contains 'for _, name := range b.Reviewer { d, ok := b.Timeout(name); if !ok { continue } ... }' to walk the reviewer chain and drop entries with no config key. internal/cli/facts.go:127-137 (reviewerBackends) reimplements the identical walk-and-skip shape to build the ordered []decide.ReviewerBackend list instead of extending config.Backends with one shared iterator (e.g. a method returning the ordered {name, timeout} pairs) that both ReviewBudgetTimeout and reviewerBackends could consume. The two callers produce different outputs (max vs. ordered list) so this is not a bug, but it is the same predicate — 'a chain entry counts only if Backends.Timeout reports true' — encoded twice in two packages.

candidates.title: backendDeadlines' defensive/malformed-payload branches are never exercised by any test
candidates.detail: backendDeadlines has four distinct guard branches for a `backends` ctx entry that isn't the shape decide.go writes: the whole value not being []any (line 371-374), an element not being map[string]any (377-379), a missing/empty key (381-384), and a present key with a missing/empty timeout — which produces the untested 'named but no deadline' rendering `` `key` `` with no '(now …)' suffix (line 385-389). Every case in TestReviewErrorNamesTheBackendTimeouts and the round-trip test only ever feeds backendDeadlines well-formed output of backendsContext (either non-empty entries with both key and timeout, or a genuinely empty list), so none of these four branches is independently verified. They're documented as defensive rather than a second code path, so this is low risk, but a regression that broke the type assertions or the no-timeout fallback formatting would go uncaught.

verdicts.evidence: config.go's Backends.ReviewBudgetTimeout and facts.go's new reviewerBackends both walk b.Reviewer and apply the identical skip predicate: config.go:118-122 reads `for _, name := range b.Reviewer { d, ok := b.Timeout(name); if !ok { continue } ...` and facts.go:129-133 reads the same four lines verbatim (`for _, name := range b.Reviewer { d, ok := b.Timeout(name); if !ok { continue }`) before diverging into a max-tracking accumulator vs. an ordered-list append. No shared iterator exists in config.Backends beyond the single-entry Timeout(name) accessor, and neither plan.md's task list, its 'Plan review findings' disposition table, nor plan.index.json task 5's description scope any follow-up to unify the two walks — task 1 deliberately adds Backends.Timeout(name) and Backends.ReviewBudgetTimeout() as the two owners, and task 5 builds reviewerBackends directly on Timeout(name) without referencing ReviewBudgetTimeout. The duplicated walk-and-skip shape is real and unmitigated, though it is exactly the low-severity duplication the candidate itself describes, not a behavioural bug.

backendDeadlines has four guard branches — ctx[ctxBackends] not []any (questions.go:371-374), an element not map[string]any (377-379), a missing/empty key (381-384), and a present key with a missing/empty timeout falling back to a bare `key` with no '(now …)' suffix (385-389). Tracing every test that reaches this function: TestReviewErrorNamesTheBackendTimeouts' three cases (two entries, one entry, nil chain) and TestReviewErrorRendersIdenticallyAfterAContextRoundTrip all build ctx['backends'] via decide.go:457-127's backendsContext, which for a non-empty chain always emits a well-formed map[string]any with both non-empty key and timeout, and for a nil chain emits an empty-but-still-[]any slice (`make([]any, 0, len(bs))` with bs=nil ranges zero times) — so the nil-chain case only exercises the len(raw)==0 fallthrough, never the isList/isMap/hasKey/hasTimeout false branches. No test anywhere in internal/decide constructs a ctx['backends'] value of the wrong type or a malformed map (grep for ctxBackends/"backends" in internal/decide shows only the two production write sites and the one read site). plan.index.json task 5's description explicitly frames this as 'defensive, not a second code path' and scopes only the three well-formed-shape test rows (keyed set, one-entry, empty set) — no task adds coverage for the malformed branches, so the gap is real and unmitigated, matching the candidate's own low-risk framing.
